method: Complete bilingual reading of all 1,093 queued event and background long texts in queue order, source and translation aligned branch by branch on the " | " separators so that every {a|b} random branch was compared with its own English. Checked meaning, subject and relationship, added or dropped sense, puns, idioms and translationese. Most entries were already faithful and fluent and were left unchanged; only confirmed errors and a few clear inconsistencies (the divine pronoun 祂) were corrected with minimal local edits. Variables, colour/img markup, numbers and branch separators were kept and every change passed core.l10n_tokens.validate_translation; the whole catalog was re-validated and passed core.l10n_style before writing.

narrative_a.scope: Round-2 continuation queue "narrative_a": 546 event and character background long texts.
boundaries: Static bilingual reading only; the game was not started and no in-game layout was checked.
Northern/southern variants and repeated event screens were each read and corrected per key.
Independent work from the original English only; no third-party (Fox) translation, glossary or script was used.

changes.source: {Raised by thieves on a diet of honeymilk and stolen gold, %name% started life off on the wrong foot. | Raised by a drunken father and an ill mother, %name% was parented straight into a life of thievery. | Born as the sixth-child of an already impoverished family, the budding thief %name% first learned the craft by stealing the last bits of dinner. | Growing up in a family servant to a rich noble, the eventual-thief %name% spent many years staring at royal opulence - and stealing from it. | Taken in by a local orphanage, it wasn't long for %name% to start taking abuse from the lowly orphans. He fell back on thieving to survive. | Orphaned, %name% grew up as a street urchin, his days governed by cutting purses and picking pockets. | While never particularly in need of money, %name%'s jealousy over material things led him to thieving. | The profligacy of the rich amidst crowds of poor always rubbed %name% the wrong way. So he stole from them both and gave to himself. | %name%'s father taught him all there was to know about stealing including, unfortunately, how to backstab. | The church steals with a silver plate. The lords do it with the taxman. So %name% figured why can't he do it with his own two hands? | Impoverished while growing up, %name% took to stealing bread. Well-fed, he soon took to stealing crowns.} {After years of successful stealing, one mistake landed %name% in a dungeon. Thankfully, years of stealing also meant years of lockpicking and he didn't spend long. | But when he was caught trying to steal a temple's chalice, a talk with a priest convinced %name% to perhaps take a different path. | Unfortunately, a smash-and-grab at a local store ended with %name% being caught red-handed. He was soon profiled on posters everywhere, making his work difficult. | Daring to cut the purse of a fat trader, %name% soon found himself nursing a hand absent of a few fingers. He really liked those fingers, too. | %name%'s thievery eventually placed him at the head of an entire guild. But after a dozen failed assassination attempts, the thief realized there was nobody to trust in his line of work. | Partnering up with a beautiful woman, %name% managed to steal from everybody. Too bad the woman stole from him, in the end. | Trying to sell some goods, a trusted fence turned out to be a traitorous informant. One bad pillory experience later and the thief was exiled from %randomtown%. | It was the perfect heist. That's all that is said about it. Now, %name% just needs to lay low. | Tortured by a rival gang, he came to miss a number of teeth, fingernails, and any drive to return to thieving. | His time as a thief came to an end when, arrested, he spent five days pilloried during tomato season. | Naturally, it wasn't long until he went to prison. He doesn't speak of his time there, but it is obvious he wishes to never return. | But one day he learned there are much better ways to spin a blade for a coin than petty thievery. | But his half-brother was captured by a local gang, forcing the thief to find new ways to pay the hefty ransom. | But life as a brigand is not easy. Arrested for eating a chicken that was not his, the man forfeited two fingers and any will to keep thieving. | After a heist went south, the man fingered all his former partners to save his own hide. Now he can never go back to thieving.} {For all you know %name% is just using sellswords to hide behind. Regardless of his reasons, he's still going to have to earn his pay. | You recognize %name% from some posters.  Well, a man who has gotten this far without being caught must have some value. | With one hand, %name% twirls a blade between his fingers. With the other, he snags your purse. Impressive. Now give it back. | Years of thieving have made %name% adept at escaping trouble. | %name% has the skills to be a good mercenary, just be sure to watch your purse while around him. | You can't trust a man like %name%, but that attribute has plenty of company anyway. | Supposedly, somebody once shot an arrow at %name%. They missed, but the thief kept the feathers. | %name%'s effort to join sellswords better not be a scheme to steal from your coffers. | Wanted posters say %name% is considered 'armed and dangerous'. Perfect. | There are plenty of lawmen looking for %name%. Maybe you can get them to join, too.}
changes.before: {%name%从小由盗贼抚养，喝着蜜乳，花着偷来的金子，人生一开始便走歪了。 | %name%有个酗酒的父亲和患病的母亲，这样的家境把他直接推上了偷窃之路。 | 家里本已穷困，%name%又是第六个孩子。这个小贼最早学会的本事，就是偷走晚饭最后的几口残羹。 | %name%一家在富有贵族家中当仆役。他多年看着贵族挥霍无度，也多年从中顺手牵羊，终于成了惯偷。 | %name%被当地孤儿院收留后，没多久就受到了其他孤儿的欺凌。他只好靠偷窃求生。 | %name%自幼失去双亲，在街头长大，日子离不开割钱袋、掏口袋。 | %name%其实从不怎么缺钱，可对别人财物的嫉妒，还是把他引上了偷窃之路。 | 穷人遍地，富人却挥霍无度，这让%name%怎么看都不顺眼。于是他两边都偷，钱全归自己。 | %name%的父亲教会他偷窃的全部本领，其中很不幸地也包括了如何背后捅刀。 | 教会拿着银盘子偷，领主靠着税吏偷。%name%心想，自己凭两只手偷，怎么就不行？ | %name%小时候穷得叮当响，便开始偷面包。等到吃饱了，很快又开始偷克朗。} {多年行窃无往不利，一次失手却让%name%进了地牢。所幸，多年偷窃也练就了开锁的本领，他没待多久便跑了。 | %name%偷神殿的圣杯时被抓了个正着，与一位祭司的一番谈话，让他觉得也许该换条路走。 | 可惜，%name%砸抢本地商店时被当场逮住。很快，四处都贴满了他的画像，生意便难做了。 | %name%胆敢去割一个胖商人的钱袋，结果没多久，就只能捂着少了几根手指的伤手。偏偏那几根手指，他还挺喜欢。 | %name%靠偷窃一路做到了整个公会的头目。可十几次未遂刺杀过后，他终于明白，干这行谁也靠不住。 | %name%与一个美貌女子搭伙，把能偷的人全偷了个遍。可惜最后，那女人又把他也偷了个精光。 | 他找一个信得过的销赃人出货，没想到对方竟是告密者。吃够了枷号的苦头后，他被逐出了%randomtown%。 | 那是一次完美的盗窃。除此之外，再没人透露半句。眼下，%name%只想避避风头。 | 他遭到敌对帮派拷打，丢了好几颗牙、好几片指甲，也丢尽了重操旧业的念头。 | 他被捕后，赶上番茄成熟的季节，在枷台上足足示众五天。他的盗贼生涯也就此结束。 | 不出所料，他没多久便进了监狱。他不肯说里面发生过什么，但显然再也不愿回去。 | 可有一天，他发现，用刀挣钱还有比小偷小摸好得多的路子。 | 可他同父或同母的兄弟被当地帮派抓走了。为了凑齐高昂的赎金，他得另找财路。 | 可盗贼的日子并不好过。他吃了不属于自己的鸡，被抓之后，丢了两根手指，也彻底丢了继续偷窃的兴致。 | 一次行动失败后，他为保全自己，供出了所有旧日同伙。从此，这一行再也容不下他。} {说不定%name%只是拿佣兵身份作掩护。无论动机如何，该干的活他还是得干，工钱可不能白拿。 | 你在几张告示上见过%name%。不过，一个逃到今天还没被逮住的人，总有些本事。 | %name%一只手在指间转着匕首，另一只手便顺走了你的钱袋。了不起。现在还回来。 | 多年的偷窃生涯，让%name%很擅长脱身避祸。 | %name%的身手足以成为优秀的佣兵，只是和他待在一起时，最好看紧钱袋。 | %name%这样的人信不过，不过这点他倒也不孤单。 | 据说，有人曾朝%name%射过一箭。人没射中，箭羽却被他顺走了。 | 最好别让%name%加入佣兵的打算，变成从你钱箱里下手的诡计。 | 通缉令说，%name%“携有武器，极度危险”。正合适。 | 有不少执法者在找%name%。也许你还能把他们一并招来。}

changes.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]{You ask the man if the North has seen any devastating wars. He shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%Aye, we've our differences. This spat and that. But a century ago a collective of warriors was formed to defeat a horde of undead. Ohh ya, see it in yer eyes that ye didn't know that one. It is likely that if they were defeated the walking corpses would have flooded south and killed you all. You're welcome. Bet they don't teach that in your fancy southern scripts.%SPEECH_OFF% | The man snorts and nods at the fishing pole.%SPEECH_ON%They say there's large fish down under there. Harmless ones, but big enough to spur the imagination. I can't say I've seen them in the flesh, but there was a time when a large shadow passed beneath my feet, passed right there through the waters, and it passed and passed, felt like forever. And then it was gone.%SPEECH_OFF%You ask how he thinks it a harmless beast. He shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%Cause it didn't do nothing but go from there to there and onward still.%SPEECH_OFF% | The man tests a fishing pole then crouches on his haunches. He nods across the ice.%SPEECH_ON%Ol' white bears will cross these stretches. Gotta keep your mind out for 'em. A bit of fire will fend them off, that or you dump your fish and make a run for it. I'd known a man who got eaten by a white bear. They said it ate him from legs up, giving no shits about his screaming and hollering. I'd sooner slit my own throat than let one of them beasts get a hold of me.%SPEECH_OFF% | A friendly enough fellow, the man rests beside his fishing poles and speaks to the nature of his own people.%SPEECH_ON%I'd been close enough south to know you think us savages. That's quite alright, but there's more to it than that, or less I suppose. We got less. Far less. And make do with it anyhow.%SPEECH_OFF%You remark that northerners frequent the south only to rape and pillage what it has. The man shrugs.%SPEECH_ON%And you send war parties north to treat us to a sense of southern justice. Seems fair enough. Nobody's doing nothing that don't have a bit of retribution hanging there clear as day to see. We're all on level.%SPEECH_OFF% | As you set beside the man he catches a fish and yanks it onto the ice. He grasps it with a fur-gloved hand and smashes its head to stop its flopping. He talks as he guts and salts it.%SPEECH_ON%Some of the northerners figured out a way to tame them giants, the unholds I think you call them.  Don't ask me how. Anytime I'd heard of a giant going anywhere all it did was kill anyone in its path and eat all the livestock.%SPEECH_OFF% | The man snorts and tests his fishing rods and sighs when there's no pull.%SPEECH_ON%I went south a few years back. Stayed there a few years just as well. That's how I know your tongue so well. When I was down that way, I tasted what you call vegetables. Disgusting things, truly, and the south wonders how we grow so big and strong up there in these wastes? I'll tell ya, we can't grow no fucking vegetables. Only thing we eat has to die and nothing with a heartbeat is willing to die easy.%SPEECH_OFF% | The friendly northern fisherman tells you stories of how the tribes come and go.%SPEECH_ON%I'll say this much, we're only run by the strong, but a strong man is only as good as his health and constitution. When he gets old, he loses both. When he gets old, he therefore loses. And so the new strong man comes to power, and with it a shattering of the tribe's history and successes. I do in part envy the southerner's sense of greater purpose, and the southerner's ability to hide his power, to stock it at arm's length so that others must do more than just swing a sword to get it from him. I tell you this in truth, and only here, as far away from my countrymen as I can be. You'll never hear me say any of this around no ordinary campfire, understand?%SPEECH_OFF%}
changes.before: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]{你问那人，北方是否经历过毁灭性的战争。他耸耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%是啊，我们也有纷争，这一场，那一场。不过，一百年前，各路战士曾聚到一起，打败了一支亡灵大军。噢，对，看你的眼神就知道，这事你没听过。要是他们败了，那些会走路的尸体大概早已涌向南方，把你们全杀光。不用谢。我打赌，你们南方那些花哨的典籍可不教这个。%SPEECH_OFF% | 那人哼了一声，朝鱼竿点点头。%SPEECH_ON%听说下面有大鱼。无害，可大得足够让人胡思乱想。我没亲眼看过全貌，不过有一回，一大片影子从我脚下游过，就从那片水里，游啊，游啊，仿佛永远也游不完。然后，就没了。%SPEECH_OFF%你问他，凭什么觉得那东西无害。他耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%因为它什么都没干，只是从那边游到这边，又接着往前游。%SPEECH_OFF% | 那人试了试鱼竿，蹲下来，朝冰面另一头点头。%SPEECH_ON%白熊会横穿这一片，得留神。弄点火能赶走它们，或者扔下鱼，拔腿就跑。我认识一个被白熊吃了的人。听说从腿开始往上吃，根本不在乎他怎么哭喊。我宁可自己割喉，也不想落进那种畜生手里。%SPEECH_OFF% | 这人颇为友善，坐在鱼竿旁，说起自己族人的秉性。%SPEECH_ON%我去过够靠南的地方，知道你们把我们当野人。没关系，不过其中还有别的缘由，或者该说，更少的缘由。我们拥有的少，少得多，可也得想法子活下去。%SPEECH_OFF%你指出，北方人常来南方，干的却只是奸淫掳掠。那人耸肩。%SPEECH_ON%而你们派军队北上，让我们领教南方的正义。看着挺公平。谁干的事，都明摆着有一份报复在后头等着。大家彼此彼此。%SPEECH_OFF% | 你在那人身旁坐下时，他恰好钓起一条鱼，甩到冰面上。他用戴毛皮手套的手抓住鱼，砸碎脑袋，不让它再扑腾，一边剖腹撒盐，一边说。%SPEECH_ON%有些北方人琢磨出了驯服巨人的办法，我想，你们叫它们巨魔。别问我是怎么做到的。我每次听说巨人去了哪里，都只有杀光挡路的人、吃光牲口这回事。%SPEECH_OFF% | 那人哼了一声，试试鱼竿，没感觉到咬钩，便叹了口气。%SPEECH_ON%几年前我去过南方，还待了几年，所以你们的话，我说得这么熟。那时候，我尝过你们所谓的蔬菜。恶心，真恶心。南方人还纳闷，我们怎么能在这些荒地里长得又高又壮？告诉你吧，我们种不出他娘的蔬菜。能吃的东西都得先杀死，而有心跳的东西，没有哪个肯轻易去死。%SPEECH_OFF% | 友善的北方渔夫，向你讲起部落如何兴起，又如何消亡。%SPEECH_ON%我只能这么说，我们只听强者的。可强者的本事，也只撑得到他身体还结实、精力还旺盛的时候。一老，两样都没了。一老，也就输了。新的强者掌权，部落过去的历史和成就，往往也跟着碎掉。我有一点羡慕南方人，能为更长远的目标打算；也羡慕他们把权力藏起来，放在别人够不着的地方，让人想夺走时，不只是挥一剑那么简单。我说的都是真心话，可只会在这里说，离同胞越远越好。在寻常篝火边，你绝不可能听见我说这些，懂吗？%SPEECH_OFF%}

changes.source: {Pushed out of his town by war, %name% wanders the world as a vagabond. | Lazy and unmotivated, %name% one day put all three of his belongings into a knapsack and hit the road. | Never a strong learner in school, %name% dropped out to wander the earth. | %name% did not have the business acumen to protect his inheritance from debtors, lawmen, and other maleficent men. Now he wanders with the last of his crowns jangling in a pocket. | Life on the road has taught %name% to be a jack of all trades, and a master of none - except walking, of course. | Not quite one for the city, and not quite one for the wild, %name% spends his purposeless days traveling between both. | During his drinking days, %name% managed to gamble away a small fortune. Now homeless, he simply wanders. | When his wife was murdered while he was away, %name% refused to sleep in the house. The man walks the earth, trying to forget the memory. | His son murdered five others. In shame, %name% abandoned his hometown to walk the earth and forget his failures as a father.} {But when a gang of thieves took all he had - including his shoes - he knew he needed yet another change. | But when he came to a literal fork in the road, the man realized he hadn't eaten in some time. His stomach demanded a change in scenery - and diet. | Sadly, the world is not a pleasant place for those who nobody would miss. He was harassed and bullied every day. | After one particularly harsh day trudging through mud, he realized there was no life to be had in walking around. | Strangely, one day he came across his long-forgotten brother he-never-had who said there was plenty of walking to be done for a mercenary outfit - and they'd pay him to do it, too! | Like any good, impulsive man, he flipped a coin on whether or not to try his hand at mercenary work.} {He's not particularly good at anything, but %name% has seen and done a lot, and that's worth at least something. | Mucking about this violent land and surviving with all his limbs is a lot more than some folks can say. | A mercenary band would be but another adventure for a vagabond like %name%. One hopes he survives to write about it. | Through his travels his only weapon was a walking stick. Let's see how he does with something a smidge sharper. | A thief, a scoundrel, a baker, a tailor, %name%'s done it all. Too bad he was never good at any of those things. Maybe it'll be different this time. | The world has been harsh to %name% for many years now. That isn't going to change, but at least he will be with brothers now.}
changes.before: {战争将%name%赶出家乡，他就此成了四处漂泊的流浪汉。 | %name%懒散又没志气，有一天把全部三件家当往背包里一塞，便上路了。 | %name%上学时就不怎么开窍，后来索性退学，四处游荡。 | %name%不懂经营，没能保住自己的遗产，任由欠债者、差役和其他恶人将它吞光。如今他四处流浪，口袋里只剩最后几枚克朗叮当作响。 | 流浪的生活让%name%什么都会一点，却什么都不精——当然，走路除外。 | 城里容不下他，野外也不完全适合他，%name%便在两者之间来回游荡，漫无目的地度日。 | 酗酒的那些年，%name%把一笔不小的家财赌了个精光。如今无家可归，只剩四处流浪。 | 外出期间，妻子遭人杀害，%name%此后再也不肯在那间屋里睡觉。他走遍天下，想忘掉那段记忆。 | 他的儿子杀了五个人。羞愧之下，%name%离开故乡，浪迹天涯，想忘掉自己做父亲的失败。}{可一伙贼抢光了他的全部东西，连鞋都没留下，他便知道，自己还得再换种活法。 | 可有一天，他在路上真捡到一把叉子，才想起自己已经很久没吃东西。肚子要求他换个地方，也换换饭食。 | 可惜，对那些死了也无人惦念的人，世界从不友善。他每天都受人骚扰、欺凌。 | 在泥泞中跋涉了格外艰难的一天后，他明白，光靠四处走路，实在过不出什么日子。 | 奇怪的是，一天他遇见了一个早被自己忘光、实际上压根没有的兄弟。对方说，佣兵战团有的是路让他走，而且还给钱！ | 和任何一个说干就干的汉子一样，他抛了枚硬币，决定要不要去当佣兵。}{%name%没什么拿手本事，可见得多、做得也多，这总归值点什么。 | 在这片暴力横行的土地上混来混去，还能四肢齐全地活着，已经比不少人强了。 | 对%name%这样的流浪汉而言，佣兵战团不过是另一场冒险。但愿他能活着将它写下来。 | 一路走来，他唯一的武器就是手杖。给他换个稍微锋利些的，看看会怎样。 | 贼、无赖、面包师、裁缝，%name%什么都干过。可惜，哪一样都没干好。也许这回会不同。 | 这世界多年来一直苛待%name%，以后也不会改变，不过至少，如今他身边有了弟兄。}

changes.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_163.png[/img]{%SPEECH_START%May our paths be gilded in the days to come.%SPEECH_OFF%The priest speaks loudly to his congregation.%SPEECH_ON%I ask of you, faithful, where is the light brightest?%SPEECH_OFF%A throng of peasants murmur about themselves. Finally, the priest holds his hand up.%SPEECH_ON%It is upon the horizon, fighting against the shade of the earth herself, that we find the Gilder's gleam to be its fiercest. And we are now fighting against the shade, and the horizon is not the earth, but the improprieties of the northern stock who dare to profane the holy lands!%SPEECH_OFF%The crowd, once confused, is suddenly unified, seemingly all too knowledgeable about religious war. The priest grins.%SPEECH_ON%That is right, I see your hearts burn with the fire of the Gilder already! We must defend the sacred grounds no matter the cost!%SPEECH_OFF%Again, the crowd roars. You're not sure what to make of the peoples themselves, but if there's one thing you know about war it is that it is good for business and a bit of holy fury might make it all the better. | The Vizier has made a rare appearance for the plebs of his land, and beside him is the greater councils of nearby cities. But he does not speak. A man clothed in gold steps forward instead.%SPEECH_ON%The path of us all has been gilded, has it not?%SPEECH_OFF%Far less gleaming than the priest, the crowd murmur amongst themselves, though none dare to contradict the holy man's assertion. The priest continues.%SPEECH_ON%The Gilder has spoken to many of us, and revealed to us a new event threat: the northerners, spurred by their so-called old gods, have swept south. They entertain the thought of a crusade! To come here, right here, and take all our lands and sacred grounds. You see, the Gilder's shine shows us the path, but perhaps to others it is far too blinding. These northerners do not understand, but we will teach them, and by the Gilder's fire we shall!%SPEECH_OFF%The crowd roars to life and any sense of hesitancy is long gone. changes.before: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_26.png[/img]老渔夫%fisherman%向弟兄们讲起往昔捕鱼的故事，逗得众人兴致盎然。%SPEECH_ON%{就这么大！我拿我娘发誓！那鱼大得，给它拽出水的时候，整条河都浅了一英尺！ | 大海是头野兽，是啊。头顶的天空是它的主人，风是牵它的绳，而我们这些人，不过是跳蚤。 | 我迷航啦！整整漂了一个夏天，海水像追猎似的灌透全船，每一道浪都带走一个水手，最后只剩我一个。没错，没错！千真万确！到了秋天，我才重新看见陆地。看见树木、群山，还有在它们上空栖居的飞鸟，我高兴得直接把船撞上礁石，扑过去亲吻沙滩，碎木就在身旁漂。那是我这辈子最快乐的一天。 | 大白鲸没见过，可绿鲸？见过。它披着一身苔藓，简直是从陆地偷来的毛皮。我们靠长矛和老水手的胆气追上了它。可惜，%randomname%——那可是鱼叉掷得最准的人——一叉扎中了喷水孔，它这才发现我们骑在背上。我不知道鲸竟能转身那么快，可它就是转了，三两下便毁掉我们的船，发狠报复，淹死了好些水手。 | 我有次钓到一条鲈鱼，大概，喏，这么大。信不信？好吧，是这么大。行，也许这么大。好吧，我没钓过鲈鱼。行了！我连鲈鱼都没见过！我只知道肯定有这种鱼！别缠着我，你们这些旱鸭子！老子是在大海上捕鱼的！你们那破池塘里的事，我一概不懂。当然，鲈鱼除外，这我还是懂的。}%SPEECH_OFF%

changes.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_182.png[/img]{You order the company into the moon-like escarpment. Suddenly, a man wearing a tall black helm swings himself around a statue. It is in the warmth of mothering that one finds the primal instincts, the flashes of intellect which all creatures, from the feeblest worms to the most soaring birds, understand, and without which man shall never have supremacy over all things. I, a man, am mother now. I, a man, have broken the order, and on this instinct native to all creatures, I shall rise, wombless, ascending above the architecture of nature herself, and become nurturer to all! I, the Grand Diviner, the one who shall moisten this dry earth with manifestations...%SPEECH_OFF%Monologuing madmen wielding strange staffs rarely have good intentions. You draw your sword and, seeing your blade, the Grand Diviner goes quiet. He nods and swings his arms wide, a flash of green sparking from his staff. Creatures like those you’ve seen before – gelatinous, bulbous assemblages of vague appendages – all start shuffling out from behind the statues. More yet encircle the entire company, occupying spaces on high, saddling themselves onto the lip of the escarpments like visitors in a coliseum, ever-ready to watch a good fight. The Grand Diviner grins and points his staff at you.%SPEECH_ON%Smile, sellsword, for when you die I shall mother you back into this world, and you shall find nurture in the bosom of my power!%SPEECH_OFF%}
changes.before: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_182.png[/img]{你命战团进入那片月牙般的陡壁。突然，一个戴高耸黑盔的男人从雕像后转了出来。他挥着一根奇特法杖，玻璃般的杖顶后拖着绿雾。%SPEECH_ON%欢迎！你们是来领会我的造诣的吗？唯有在母性的温暖中，才能找到最原始的本能，那一道智慧的闪光。从最孱弱的蠕虫，到翱翔最高的飞鸟，一切生灵都懂得它；没有它，人类绝无法凌驾万物。我，一个男人，如今已成为母亲。我，一个男人，打破了秩序！凭借所有生灵与生俱来的本能，我将崛起，无需子宫，超越自然本身的构造，成为万物的养育者！我，大先知，将以造物滋润这片干涸的大地……%SPEECH_OFF%挥着古怪法杖、喋喋自语的疯子，向来少有好意。你拔出剑。看见剑刃，大先知安静下来，点头张开双臂，杖上闪出一道绿光。那些你曾见过的生物——胶质般臃肿，由模糊肢体拼成的怪物——开始从雕像后缓缓走出。更多怪物则将整支战团围住，占据高处，跨坐在陡壁边缘，像竞技场里随时准备欣赏恶斗的观众。大先知咧嘴笑着，将法杖指向你。%SPEECH_ON%笑吧，佣兵！等你死后，我将如母亲般让你重返世间，在我力量的怀抱中，得到哺育！%SPEECH_OFF%}

changes.source: [img]gfx/ui/events/event_03.png[/img]{You come over a sand dune to see a half dozen men. They are wearing black cloaks and have their sleeve-sheathed hands holding onto one another to form a complete circle. Despite every one of their heads being down, they all seem to sense your presence and turn to stare. One man lets his hands go and steps forward.%SPEECH_ON%Davkul awaits us all, traveler, even the gilded path permits his patience.%SPEECH_OFF%}

changes.source: {Burly and with churchbells for fists, %name% has spent much of the past year sharpening his boxing skills on the grindstone that is his fellow man. | With a face contorted to the shapes of others' knuckles, it's not hard to realize that %name% is a career fighter. | %name% loves the drink as much as he does a good fight, a potent combination. | A hard upbringing by his father and brothers honed %name% into being a temperamental fighter. | Bullies in %name%'s spriteful youth forged him into a man that prefers to seek out a fight rather than wait for it to come to him.  | %name% only ever had one real talent: using his fists to bloody the noses of other men and not going down no matter what. | Growing up, %name% wrestled bulls on the family farm. Unfortunately for men, he found time to venture into the cities.} {For the past year he has been employed by a local lord, paraded around to fistfight the champions of royalty. | A lover of the bar brawl, the man has apparently been banned from too many taverns to count. | Gaining notoriety as a fighter in %randomtown% meant he had to fight every single proud, boasting, and drunk man who came his way. | Although he became an undefeated prizefighter, he was hardly earning enough to get by. | Fiery in spirit, he's always willing to take up fisticuffs. changes.source: {The gods pity men, spurring many, not unlike %name%, to seek their favor. | Illiterate and born to poverty, %name% found refuge in tales of the gods. | Always a man to devour books, it wasn't long until %name% discovered texts of the gods. | Some say the gods speak to us and, if true, they definitely spoke to %name%. | With new cults springing up in the wilds, %name% returned to the familiarity of the gods. | Raised by his firebrand father, %name% spent much of his early years nursing wounds from good floggings. The gods would approve.} {When war came to the land, the gods told him to take part for greater justice. | As cultists spread their vile word like disease on a rat, %name% saw fit to take up arms and battle the heresy. | Straying from his faith, he committed a horrific crime in %randomtown% - finding company with a man. While flagellating himself nightly, he seeks redemption. | Hearing but a mere rumor of a holy place, the pilgrim took up staff and supplies to seek it out. | Now that war has returned to the land, the gods' devotee wished to find out why, through prayer and corporeal means. | A night spent in a cave revealed to the believer that the gods demanded blood. %name% was not one to refuse their beckoning. | After raiders looted the coffers of his church, %name%'s quest was to refill the pure purses.} {As the laws of the universe bend to a world-consuming war, a thaumaturge like %name% might be useful to have around. | He carries a whip with glass-barbed leather. This is not for your enemies, he states, but for purity. Interesting. | He professes to hate evil, but for a few crowns %name% can be persuaded to make anything 'evil'. | This man seeks the difficult road, no doubt why he saw fit to join a mercenary band. | If %name% had the power, you believe he'd purge the entire world. Thankfully, he is a mere man. | Talks of the gods might be a tad irksome, but %name%'s fiery passion lends itself well to the battlefield. | So enamored with the world of the gods, it's not much of a surprise that the pilgrim sees the real one filled with enemies.}
changes.before: {诸神怜悯世人，许多人因此寻求神恩，%name%也不例外。 | %name%出身贫寒，目不识丁，却从诸神的传说中寻得了慰藉。 | %name%向来如饥似渴地读书，没过多久便读到了诸神的经文。 | 有人说，诸神会对凡人说话。若这是真的，他们肯定对%name%说过。 | 新兴邪教在荒野中接连冒头，%name%却回归了自己熟悉的诸神信仰。 | %name%由狂热的父亲养大，早年的许多时日都在养伤——那些伤来自一顿又一顿结实的鞭打。诸神想必很赞许。}{战火烧到这片土地时，诸神告诉他，要为更大的正义投身其中。 | 邪教徒像老鼠传播瘟疫一样散布邪说，%name%便觉得该拿起武器，与异端作战。 | 他曾背离信仰，在%randomtown%犯下“骇人的罪行”——与一名男子相好。如今他夜夜鞭笞自己，寻求救赎。 | 仅仅听到一点圣地的传闻，这位朝圣者便拿起手杖，带上补给，踏上寻访之路。 | 战争再次降临大地，这位虔诚的信徒想通过祈祷与肉身苦修，弄清其中缘由。 | 在山洞中度过的一夜，让这名信徒领悟到诸神渴求鲜血。%name%绝不会拒绝他们的召唤。 | 掠夺者洗劫了教堂的钱箱后，%name%便肩负起使命，要重新填满这只圣洁的钱袋。}{吞噬世界的战争仿佛连天地法则都能扭曲，身边留个%name%这样的神秘行者，也许会有用。 | 他带着一条皮鞭，上面嵌着玻璃倒刺。他说，这不是给敌人准备的，而是为了净化自身。有意思。 | 他口口声声痛恨邪恶，不过只要给几个克朗，就能说服%name%把任何东西都当成“邪恶”。 | 这人专挑难走的路，也难怪他会看上佣兵队伍。 | 要是%name%真有那个本事，你相信他会把全世界都净化一遍。所幸，他不过是一介凡人。 | 他满嘴诸神，或许有点烦人，不过%name%的狂热倒很适合战场。 | 这位朝圣者一心沉醉于诸神的世界，自然会觉得现实世界处处都是敌人。}
